description: The production floor under every dev-only surface in this app: nothing above it may appear in a production build, whatever else is asked for. Held separately from `codeyamLaunched` because the two dev-only surfaces need different amounts — the agent panel is summoned per tab by a person on their own server and needs only this floor, while the component fixtures must additionally know codeyam started the server. Sharing the floor and nothing else keeps the production rule written once without forcing either surface to adopt the other's gate; `agentPanelRequested` previously carried an inline copy of it.
name: devSurfacesPermitted

description: Takes the LAST non-empty line of a Prisma message, which is the diagnosis - The column X does not exist in the current database. Deliberately not the first line: a Prisma message opens with its own framing (Invalid prisma.thinkingMap.findUnique() invocation:), so taking the first puts the call site on screen and leaves out the column, which is exactly backwards for someone working out what to fix.
name: diagnosisLine

description: Marks a response as a genuine fault. Deliberately narrow: a conflict or a timeout is a normal result the agent is expected to reason about, and flagging those as errors would invite the blind retry the conflict path exists to prevent.
name: errorResponse

description: The exchange log's MCP resource URI, one per map, so a subscriber is subscribed to a specific map rather than to 'the exchange' in the abstract. Kept in the file that owns every navigator.modelContext name, so the registration and the notification cannot drift to different URIs.
name: exchangeUri

untestabilityReason.justification: a single template string with no branching or input handling; the URI shape is exercised through its only two callers, bindExchangeResource and notifyExchangeUpdated, whose own behaviour is platform-glue against an unshipped browser API

description: Expands any IPv6 form — :: compression, a zone id, an embedded dotted-quad tail — into eight 16-bit groups, or null when it is not IPv6 at all. The embedded-IPv4 handling is what stops every blocked v4 range from passing as a v6 address.
name: expandIpv6

description: The lower-cased extension of a filename, or empty when it has none. Needed because browsers are inconsistent about the media type they attach to a .md - several send application/octet-stream - so the extension is the fallback the type dispatch falls back to.
name: extensionOf

untestabilityReason.justification: Private to a module that imports server-only plus unpdf and mammoth, so the file cannot load under vitest to reach it. Exercised end to end instead: real .pdf, .docx, .md and .txt uploads were extracted through the running app, including a .md sent as application/octet-stream, which is the case this helper exists for.

description: Posts a chosen or dropped file to /api/briefs/extract and reads the answer. The bytes go over the wire because reading a PDF is a server's job, and nothing is persisted, so a document the person discards leaves nothing behind.
name: extractBriefFromFile

untestabilityReason.justification: It builds one multipart request and delegates: every decision in it belongs to readBriefResponse, which is fully covered in app/lib/briefFetch.test.ts.

description: Gets the words out of whatever the client sent - PDF via unpdf, .docx via mammoth, HTML through extractHtmlPage, markdown and plain text decoded directly - dispatching on media type and falling back to the file extension, because browsers are inconsistent about the type they attach to a .md. The HTML branch is checked before the general text/ branch, which would otherwise claim text/html and hand the markup through as if the tags were prose. Server-only, and the single place any format-specific dependency is reached. Reads the buffer's size before extracting, since pdfjs detaches it.
name: extractBriefText

untestabilityReason.justification: The module imports server-only plus unpdf and mammoth, so it does not load under vitest at all. Its decision logic is extracted into the pure, tested extractionWarning and normalizeBriefText; what remains is dispatch and two library calls. The format paths were verified end to end against the running app with real .pdf, .docx, .md and .txt uploads, including a scanned-PDF case.

description: Pulls the raw text out of a .docx through mammoth, discarding the formatting. A brief is words; the Word file it arrived in is packaging.
name: extractDocx

untestabilityReason.justification: A wrapper around mammoth inside a server-only module that does not load under vitest. Verified against the running app with a real .docx upload, which extracted its four paragraphs intact.

description: Gets the readable article out of a web page — Readability over a linkedom document, falling back to a stripped body copy when Readability declines on a page that is not article-shaped. Opens the result with the page's own title as a markdown heading, which is what gives a page-derived brief something for the section splitter to split on and something better than boilerplate to name the board after. Lives outside briefText.ts so it can be tested at all: that module imports server-only, which throws under vitest.
name: extractHtmlPage

description: Pulls the text out of a PDF through unpdf, merging pages into one string. unpdf rather than pdf-parse because pdf-parse runs a debug branch at import that reads a fixture off disk and fails in a bundled server runtime. Note that pdfjs transfers the buffer to its worker and detaches it, so the caller must read the size first.
name: extractPdf

untestabilityReason.justification: A wrapper around unpdf inside a server-only module that does not load under vitest. Verified against the running app with two real PDFs: a healthy 924-byte document extracted 299 characters, and an 80KB document stripped of its text extracted 10 and correctly raised the scanned-PDF warning.

description: Decides whether an extraction failed and says so in a sentence the person can act on: nothing at all came out, or a large file yielded almost no text - the scanned-PDF signature. Pure and separate from the extractor so the safety net of the whole intake is testable, and because the size it takes must be measured before extraction: pdfjs transfers the upload buffer to its worker and detaches it.
name: extractionWarning

description: The colour a card's family draws its icon and its thread in, as a CSS variable reference rather than a class name — for the SVG thread layer and the icon, which need a paint value. Pro and risk resolve to their own two colours rather than a shared judgment hue, for the same reason nodeShellClasses keeps them apart: a thread rising to a risk should be the risk colour, not a family average.
name: familyLineVar

description: A node kind's colour family, via KIND_FAMILY. The twenty kinds collapse into six families because one hue per kind would be a legend rather than a system, and the eyebrow above every card already names the exact kind for anyone who wants the precision. KIND_FAMILY is a total Record on purpose, so a twenty-first kind will not compile until it is given a family; this wrapper adds the runtime half of that safety, since kinds also arrive from the database and from the model unvalidated - an unrecognised one falls back to the neutral ground family rather than losing its colour entirely.
name: familyOf

description: Where along a parent card's bottom edge each of its threads departs. Every thread starting at the same point is what turns four curves into one frayed rope — they overlap for the first stretch and only separate once already travelling sideways — so the departures are fanned evenly across the card's own bottom edge, symmetric about its centre and inset from the rounded corners. The caller passes its threads in the order of the children they land on, which is what keeps one parent's threads from crossing each other.
name: fanOrigins

description: The SVG curve from the idea out to one theme's hub. Both control points sit midway along the run, one holding the idea's horizontal and one the row's, so every branch leaves the idea flat and arrives at its row flat — which is what makes several of them read as one splaying bundle rather than as unrelated diagonals. Rim to rim rather than centre to centre, or the curve disappears under the circle it points at.
name: fanPath

description: Posts an address to /api/briefs/fetch and reads the answer. The retrieval is the server's job because CORS blocks a browser fetching almost any third-party page, and because the guard on a stranger's URL cannot live in a browser.
name: fetchBriefFromLink

untestabilityReason.justification: It builds one request and delegates: every decision in it belongs to readBriefResponse, which is fully covered in app/lib/briefFetch.test.ts, and to the route's own guard.

description: Fetches a URL while re-running the guard at every redirect hop, and reports the address that finally answered. Lives beside the guard rather than in the route that calls it precisely because redirect: 'follow' would let a permitted host bounce to 127.0.0.1 with nothing left to check — leaving the loop in a handler would mean the next route could call checkBriefUrl correctly and still reopen the hole.
name: fetchGuarded

untestabilityReason.justification: It exists to make real network requests, and this project has no HTTP-interception harness to drive redirect chains against. The per-hop decision it delegates to — checkBriefUrl, and through it isBlockedAddress — is covered in app/lib/briefUrl.test.ts; the loop itself was verified against a live http-to-https redirect.

description: Read one non-empty string field off an event payload, or null. The single guard every rail reader goes through, so an unparseable row degrades to a plainer line rather than throwing.
name: field

description: The user-origin changes to one node that landed after the revision an agent last read. Empty means the write is safe; non-empty means the person touched this node and the caller must decline instead of overwriting. Narrowed twice on purpose: an agent's own earlier writes are not a conflict with itself, and a busy map moves constantly so only a change to THIS node can clobber THIS write.
name: findConflictingChanges

description: The one definition of "have we already recorded a batch under this requestId". Returns the original batch as a deduped RecordResult so a retry sees exactly what the first attempt produced, or null when the key is new or absent - an absent key is not an error, since idempotency is opt-in and a call without one is meant to write. Takes a transaction client rather than reaching for the singleton, and that is the point: the check has to run inside the transaction that does the writing, because two checks racing outside a shared transaction can both miss and both write. Extracted so applyToolCalls and recordEvents cannot drift into two different notions of "seen this key".
name: findPriorBatch

description: Resolves a tool by name from the shared catalog. Every front door goes through it, and an unknown name comes back undefined so the caller can answer the agent rather than throw.
name: findTool

description: The text of the first answer in a user.answer payload. Only shown when a single question was answered — with several, a row has no way to say which answer belongs to which question.
name: firstAnswer

description: The first n non-empty lines of a document, for the intake's proof-of-extraction preview. Blank lines are skipped rather than counted, so a brief that opens with a heading and two blank lines still previews as three real lines.
name: firstLines

description: A character count with grouped thousands. A bare 12690 reads as an identifier sitting in a column of otherwise short numbers; grouped, it reads as an amount, which is the only reason it is shown.
name: formatCharCount

description: The standing ask, rendered as the Insights section of what read_map returns: what the board is carrying, and what is owed. This is the whole mechanism behind always-on insights. The page cannot summon an agent - that is the product's founding constraint - so the only place the ask can live is inside what the agent already reads on every turn. It states a BUDGET rather than a mood, because a number an agent can compare itself against is actionable in a way that 'consider adding insights' is not. The empty case reads as an invitation rather than a fault: a map on its first turn has no insights and has done nothing wrong, so telling it what an insight IS beats reporting a shortfall.
name: formatInsightStanding

description: Renders one map in full for an MCP client - the verbatim seed idea, the conversation, the indented node tree, and the Insights section carrying the standing ask - so a client sees both views of the thinking the way the UI shows them side by side, plus how far behind the insight budget it currently is.
name: formatMapDetail

description: Renders the map list for an MCP client, leading every row with the id because that is what the client passes back to every other tool, and saying so plainly when there are no maps yet.
name: formatMapList

description: Renders what await_new_map handed back, for an agent that arrives with no context about the map at all. Every row leads with the id and spells out the next call rather than leaving it to be inferred: read_brief when the map was started from a document, read_map otherwise. An expiry gets its own branch - no new maps yet plus the cursor to resume from - so an agent looping on this never reads the ordinary case as a failure.
name: formatNewMaps

description: Sends a page-side tool call to the tools route, where the shared runtime executes it. The page cannot run the catalog itself because every implementation ends in SQLite, so this one hop is the only difference between the page door and the two server doors.
name: forward

untestabilityReason.justification: A single fetch plus a non-2xx guard that turns a transport failure into a readable message. What it sends is decided by validateToolInput and what it receives is produced by runTool, both covered by their own entries.

description: The map route's browser-tab title. Counts the map's still-open questions into the title so a backgrounded board says how much is waiting, and falls back to the bare app name when the map is missing or the read throws — metadata runs a frame before the body, so a throw here would 500 the route before the page could explain itself.
name: generateMetadata

description: Loads a map's brief including its text - the one reader allowed to want it. Everything else takes the metadata that getMap selects, so tens of thousands of characters never reach a page render or a full read_map.
name: getBrief

untestabilityReason.justification: A one-line Prisma findUnique with no branching. The behaviour actually worth pinning is that getMap excludes the brief text while read_map still announces it, which mcpFormat.test.ts covers.

description: Loads a map's brief and returns its coverage by the nodes on that map, ready to render. The thin database half of computeBriefCoverage, kept here so that module stays pure and testable. Returns only headings and counts - never the brief's text - so rendering the panel on the server does not put a document of tens of thousands of characters on the wire. Null when the map has no brief, which the workspace renders by mounting no panel at all.
name: getBriefCoverage

description: Reads one map with its full conversation and node tree in creation order. The single read behind the workspace, the summary screen and the MCP get_thinking_map tool.
name: getMap

description: Groups a map's nodes into the rounds that produced them — one round per write, read off the exchange log, because nodes written together share a contiguous run of revisions and one origin. Deliberately NOT grouped by tree depth: an agent's second batch of questions usually lands at the same depth as its first, so by depth the two turns would collapse into one row. The root idea is always its own first round, and nodes the log never mentions fall back to depth grouping so a seeded or pre-existing map still draws.
name: groupIntoRounds

description: Sorts a finished map's nodes into the regions of the summary screen - known, unknown, directions, next steps and the build sequence's slices - ignoring every other kind and ordering each bucket by its stored order, because the steps and the slices are both numbered on screen. Slices sit beside the next steps rather than replacing them: a next step can be to interview three teachers, which is not something you build.
name: groupSummaryNodes

description: The MCP HTTP endpoint. Builds a fresh server and transport per request so concurrent clients never share transport state, then hands the request to the transport.
name: handle

untestabilityReason.justification: Four straight-line statements with no branching: construct server, construct transport, connect, delegate. The tools underneath are covered by their own entries, and the endpoint was verified end to end against a live MCP client - initialize, tools/list, and a create/add-node/read round trip.

description: What a map with nobody working on it says for itself, in words - pure, and pinned by tests rather than left as strings inside a component. `hasBrief` decides which tool the start prompt names. `worked` selects the demoted wording for a map an agent has already left, because 'No one is on this yet' is false there. `origin` builds both spellings of the MCP endpoint: the bare `<origin>/api/mcp` any agent puts in its connector settings, and `mcpCommand`, the `claude mcp add` shortcut - the HTTP form when the origin is known, `npm run mcp` on the server render where it is not. `attachTabs` returns the three ways in as alternatives rather than prose, ordered browser / any agent / Claude Code, with the browser tab carrying no copyable text at all because that route needs nothing pasted anywhere. `mcpCommand` stays flat beside them because HandoffReattach shows it with no tabs around it.
name: handoffCopy

description: Node id to the hue of the theme it belongs to. Deliberately PARTIAL: a node with no theme, a node whose theme is gone, and a node that no longer exists all simply have no entry, and the caller renders those neutrally. That is the honest treatment — a default colour would claim a theme the answer does not belong to, and an error would break a whole transcript over a card somebody deleted.
name: hueByNodeId

description: The colour of the nth theme, handed out along the golden angle from a magenta start. Colour is the board's navigation affordance — it is how you know which galaxy you are looking at once the labels are too small to read — so the promise is that the hues stay mutually distinguishable however many themes an idea turns out to need, which is what an irrational step round the wheel gives and a fixed palette cannot. Pure and total, so a theme's colour survives a reload without being stored twice.
name: hueForIndex

description: Stands in for a heading when a passage has none: the first nine words of its opening line, elided if there were more. A person scanning the outline needs to recognise the passage, not read it.
name: impliedHeading

description: The board's insights and how far behind the thinking they are, computed from the nodes alone. An insight is a node whose kind is in INSIGHT_STREAM_KINDS AND which carries no theme: a finding hung inside a theme is a card in that row, a themeless one is a claim about the whole idea. That rule already existed informally as CORE_INSIGHT_KINDS plus !n.themeId in GalaxyBoard, and promoting it here is what stops the agent's read and the browser disagreeing about what is on the board - a disagreement that would draw the same node twice or count it never. Staleness is read off timestamps rather than the exchange log, which is the decision that lets this be pure: MapNode.updatedAt moves when an answer lands, so one function serves both the server-side read_map and the client without either holding the log. Deriving it from MapEvent revisions was the alternative and would have forced a second query into read_map's delta branch on every turn. Nothing is hidden by being stale - an insight the thinking has moved past is still worth reading, and dropping it would silently shrink the board. Returns all zeros for an empty map, which is the day-one state and the one every capture produces.
name: insightStream

description: Whether a card should show your words as its content with the question demoted to their label. Only a question can reach this state: a settled insight carries an answered status all over the seed data and is still not something you answered, and drawing it with a pencil would invite editing the partner's own thinking as though it were your reply.
name: isAnsweredCard

description: Whether a resolved IP is somewhere the server refuses to fetch from: loopback, link-local (including the cloud metadata endpoint at 169.254.169.254), the private and carrier-NAT ranges, multicast and reserved space, in both IPv4 and IPv6 — unwrapping IPv4-mapped IPv6 so a blocked v4 range cannot slip through wearing a v6 hat. Pure and exported so the security boundary can be enumerated in tests rather than trusted by inspection; anything that is not a resolved address fails closed.
name: isBlockedAddress

description: Guard for the eight kinds the exchange log can record. A kind outside the set would become a row that nothing knows how to render or resume past.
name: isEventKind

description: Whether a board card is showing you something rather than asking you something. Two clauses: the node's kind is one of the partner's own thinking - which now includes suggestion and experiment, since both are the partner telling you what it would do rather than asking you anything - OR the card carries a diagram or a picture, and the second clause is the one that was missing. The layout's widthFor already hands exactly those cards the wide column on that reasoning, so without the same rule here an approach with a diagram was laid out at the wide width, drawn as an answered question, and its diagram never rendered at all.
name: isInsightCard

description: Type guard for the node kinds the map knows how to draw. Used to drop a hallucinated kind at the planning stage rather than storing a node no component has a treatment for.
name: isNodeKind

description: Type guard for the three node statuses. Status drives the visual treatment, so an unrecognised value is normalised rather than allowed to fall through to the default silently.
name: isNodeStatus

description: Whether a card is still asking something of you, and so still carries a field. The three faces are mutually exclusive and total by construction — two of them true at once would stack two bodies in one card, none of them true would render an empty box.
name: isOpenCard

description: Type guard for the five phases of the loop. SQLite has no enums, so phase strings arrive from the database and from model tool calls unvalidated; this is what keeps an unknown value out of the phase nav. It deliberately answers a NARROWER question than normalizePhase: whether a value is literally one of the five current phases, which is what the tool schema validates against. A stored phase from before deconstruct and map merged is not one of them, and goes through normalizePhase instead.
name: isPhase

description: Whether a round is mostly research, finding or gap — the rule that decides which row gets its own banded territory rather than just its own card colour. Strictly more than half, so an even split does not band: a round with no majority has nothing to name it after. 'Mostly' rather than 'all' because a research round that picked up one stray question is still a research round, and demanding purity would mean the band never appeared on a real map. The root round never bands, since enclosing the map's subject as 'what already exists' would misdescribe it.
name: isResearchRound

description: Guard for the three kinds a browser is allowed to write. This is a trust boundary rather than a convenience: the page posts these directly, so accepting an agent-side kind here would let a page forge the other half of the conversation.
name: isUserEventKind

description: Whether a browser agent can actually reach this page: a model context exists, the context is secure, and the page is top level. All three are real gates - WebMCP is top-level-secure-context only, so the codeyam capture iframe fails the last one by design in every preview and scenario.
name: isWebMcpAvailable

description: The mirror of the fan: the curve from the end of a finished row back to the conclusion. Leaves from the far edge of the last card rather than its origin, so it does not run back through the card, and returns null for a row with no cards — there is no end to leave from, and a line drawn from the hub would promise a conclusion the row has not reached.
name: joinPath

description: Places the idea, the lines of thinking fanning off it, each row of question cards, and the point where the rows converge — in abstract board units, knowing nothing about pixels or zoom. Each card sits at the running sum of the widths before it rather than at an index times a constant, which is what lets a card carrying a diagram or a picture push its neighbours along instead of being drawn on top of them. The convergence clears the longest row, and an empty map still returns finite bounds so a board with nothing on it frames on something real.
name: layOutGalaxy

description: One event's worth of conversation: the per-kind switch behind chatLines. Returns a LIST because the mapping is genuinely one-to-many in both directions — a user.answer closing three cards yields three lines (three subjects cannot share one bubble's background), and node.added, theme.added or phase.set yield none, because those are things you can see on the board and narrating them would make the panel a changelog of a picture the person is already looking at. Total over anything the log can hold: a malformed payload costs its own bubble, never the whole transcript.
name: lineFor

description: Lists every thinking map newest-first with its phase and node/message counts. Backs the landing screen's Pick up where you left off list and the MCP list_thinking_maps tool.
name: listMaps

description: The stdio entrypoint for MCP clients that launch the server as a child process, such as Claude Desktop. Serves the same buildMcpServer over a stdio transport; only the transport differs from the HTTP route.
name: main

untestabilityReason.justification: A process entrypoint: build the server, connect a stdio transport, log readiness to stderr because stdout is the JSON-RPC channel. No branching. Verified by driving a real initialize and tools/list handshake through the process over a pipe.

description: The production seed entrypoint, deliberately a no-op. CodeYam projects start with an empty production database and let each scenario carry its own seed, so there is nothing to plant here.
name: main

untestabilityReason.justification: Scaffold-shipped entrypoint left as the no-op the CodeYam data model calls for: production starts empty and scenarios carry their own seeds. There is no behaviour to assert because the function deliberately does nothing.

description: Derives the line beside LIVE MAP from the current nodes so the map narrates itself truthfully: a bare seed, a count of open questions, an answered/open split, or the reassurance that nothing was lost after a direction change. Excludes the root idea from the answered count, and lets a just-updated node outrank the arithmetic.
name: mapCaption

description: Whether the map named in the URL is real, checked before either verb touches the log. Both GET and POST answer 404 rather than minting a revision against a map that does not exist.
name: mapExists

untestabilityReason.justification: A bare findUnique selecting only the id, coerced to a boolean. The work is the database call itself; the route behaviour it guards is covered by the exchange route's own probes and the mid-exchange scenario.

description: Gets a message string out of an unknown thrown value: an Error, an object carrying a string message, or the value stringified. Exists because what reaches the classifier is genuinely unknown - a throw is not obliged to throw an Error - and the screen must render something rather than crash on the way to explaining a crash.
name: messageOf

description: A node timestamp as milliseconds, for a value that may arrive as a Date from Prisma or as the ISO string a JSON round trip leaves behind - which is exactly why this module can be read by the server and the browser alike. A value it cannot parse sorts as epoch rather than NaN: NaN would make every comparison against it false, so a single bad timestamp would silently drop its node out of every count while looking like it had been considered.
name: millis

description: Reads navigator.modelContext, or null where there is none. The single place the WebMCP global is touched, so the draft spec moving again is one edit rather than a sweep.
name: modelContext

untestabilityReason.justification: A guarded read of a browser global that exists only in Chrome 146+. The availability decisions built on it - isWebMcpAvailable and webMcpUnavailableReason - are covered by app/lib/webmcp.test.ts, which stubs this same global.

description: Digs the column the driver actually named out of meta.driverAdapterError.cause.column, or returns null. Preferred over parsing the message because it is a field rather than prose and does not move when Prisma rewords itself; the message stays as the fallback, since this nesting is adapter-specific and an unfamiliar adapter may not fill it.
name: namedColumn

description: Whether a guarded write warrants reading the log at all. An unguarded write is the agent saying it does not care, and a map that has not moved cannot have a conflict, so neither case costs a read.
name: needsConflictCheck

description: Shapes the node.added event payload from the row that was just inserted. A translation, not a write: the database's vocabulary in, the exchange contract's vocabulary out. Both options and fromNodeIds are stored as JSON strings because SQLite has no array type, and the log speaks the contract's language rather than the column's, so they come back out as the arrays the tools take. The optional fields - testsNodeId, fromNodeIds, sourceRef, options - are OMITTED entirely when absent rather than sent as null, so a reader can treat presence as meaning and an ordinary node's event stays byte-for-byte what it has always been. fromNodeIds is omitted for an empty list too: an insight that cited nothing must be indistinguishable from one written before the field existed, where an empty array would instead read as 'this insight named its sources and they were none'. Pure, so it is unit-testable without a database; inline it could only be reached through a live insert.
name: nodeAddedPayload

description: The node a question is about, if it is genuinely on this map. The same ownership check mapExists makes, pushed down to the payload so a caller cannot ask about a node belonging to someone else's map; returns the label too, because the rail names the node.
name: nodeOnMap

description: Picks the shell classes for a map card, encoding the design system rule that must not break: status beats kind. The precedence is root, then updated, then open, then kind colour, then answered — so an unanswered question is dashed and unfilled whatever family it belongs to, and exactly one card wears the lime. Kind colour slots in at the accent tier and nowhere above it: pro and risk keep their own two colours because the pair points opposite ways, and every other kind takes its family line and near-white tint. The root gave up its ink FILL when the pill became a card — inverting 240px reads as a hole in the page and would take the eye before the lime card that should have it — and carries its weight with a doubled ink border instead.
name: nodeShellClasses

description: Normalises a freshly extracted brief: CRLF and bare CR become newlines, trailing spaces and tabs are stripped from every line, runs of three or more newlines collapse to one paragraph break, and the document's own outer whitespace is trimmed. Everything downstream assumes this has run, so a .docx and a paste split into the same sections.
name: normalizeBriefText

description: The phase a stored string means, following the legacy aliases. Distinct from isPhase, which answers whether a value is literally one of the five current phases: the tool schema validates against the current vocabulary, while every path that READS a stored phase has to cope with what earlier versions wrote — chiefly 'deconstruct', which resolves to 'map'. Returns null for an unrecognised string so the caller picks its own fallback rather than being handed a wrong phase.
name: normalizePhase

description: Tells a subscribed agent the log moved. Reads the hook at call time rather than capturing it at module load, so a browser that gains the capability mid-session is picked up without a reload. Purely an optimisation that removes polling latency; a notification is not a turn and nothing depends on it.
name: notifyExchangeUpdated

untestabilityReason.justification: branches entirely on navigator.modelContext.notifyResourceUpdated, an unshipped W3C proposal no browser implements; the only reachable path today is the no-op

description: Reads back the list of things brought along with an idea. Names only, and anything unreadable becomes an empty list — the rule is about availability rather than correctness: a board that cannot parse its own attachment column must still OPEN, because one stray string taking the whole page down is a far worse outcome than a board rendering without its attachments.
name: parseAttachments

description: Reads a brief off an untrusted request body. A brief with no text in it is not a brief, and every way of expressing that - missing, empty, whitespace, wrongly typed, not an object - reduces to undefined so the caller has one case rather than five. The text is kept verbatim; a missing source name or media type falls back to the pasted defaults.
name: parseBriefInput

description: The half of the SSRF guard that needs no network: parses what the person typed, assumes https when no scheme was given, and refuses anything that is not http/https or that carries credentials in the URL. Returns a normalised URL or a sentence the person can act on, never a thrown error, because a bad address is something they typed rather than a fault.
name: parseBriefUrl

description: Reads a question's shortlist back off the map. Stored as a JSON string because SQLite has no array column, so anything malformed degrades to an open-ended question rather than throwing — a card that cannot render its options is still a question worth asking, and a board that will not open is not.
name: parseChoices

description: Reads a card's drawn shape back off the map, with the same contract as parseChoices: a stored value that cannot be parsed becomes no diagram rather than an exception. The card then renders as an ordinary one, which is the right degradation — a missing shape costs a picture, a throw costs the whole board.
name: parseDiagram

description: Reads a nudge batch off a request body, returning the parsed batch or the message to send back — the caller picks the status code, this decides what is acceptable. Offsets must be FINITE, not merely numeric: NaN and Infinity are both typeof number and either would put a node nowhere. One bad entry rejects the whole batch, since a partial arrangement is harder to explain than a refused one. Vestigial along with its route: nothing produces a nudge now that the map is a scrolling column of cards.
name: parseNudges

description: Reads a question's suggested answers out of the JSON array the column stores — SQLite has no array type. A missing, malformed, or wrongly-shaped value yields no chips at all, because a question with no shortlist is the ordinary case rather than a degraded one; blank and non-string entries are dropped so no unlabelled chip is ever rendered.
name: parseOptions

description: Reads a node id out of an event payload, returning null for anything that is not a non-empty string. Keeps a malformed event from contributing a phantom id to a round.
name: payloadId

description: Reads a phase name out of a phase.set payload, returning null for anything that is not a non-empty string. Lets a round be named after the phase it opened without a malformed payload blanking the row's eyebrow.
name: payloadPhase

description: The questions a pending ask_user is waiting on. The server writes them onto the map and returns this pending shape; only the page can perform the middle step of asking a person. Returns empty for an errored call or a result carrying none, which is the signal to hand the server's response straight back - putting a prompt on screen off the back of a failure would be worse than showing nothing.
name: pendingQuestions

description: What the page may honestly claim while it waits for the next round. The shimmering placeholder row is a promise, and WebMCP is pull-only — the page cannot start an agent's turn or know one is coming — so the shimmer is bounded and resolves into one of three genuinely different sentences: an agent is working and has the answers, an agent is attached but not in a turn, or nothing can reach the page and the answers are simply on the log. Hidden while the newest round still has open questions, and at next-steps where the loop arrives. Modelled on askPresence, which does the same job for the ask composer.
name: pendingRow

description: A phase's name for use in a sentence. The phase nav numbers its labels; the rail strips the number, so a row reads 'moved to Explore' rather than 'moved to 05 Explore'.
name: phaseName

description: Turns the model's tool calls into a validated plan of map changes without touching the database. Drops nodes whose kind the map cannot draw and nodes with blank labels, normalises an unknown status to answered, preserves insert order so a parent precedes the child that names it, and ignores an out-of-range phase. Two fields are deliberately NOT resolved here and are carried through as refs for applyToolCalls to resolve: a slice's tests field, as testsRef, and an insight's fromRefs, naming the questions it came out of. Like parentRef they may name nodes created earlier in the same call, so resolving them belongs to applyToolCalls, which can see the ids the database just handed back.
name: planMapMutations

description: Records something the person did onto the map's log. The tools run in the browser but the log lives in SQLite, so an answer only becomes durable - and only becomes visible to an agent on another front door - once it has come back through this route.
name: postUserEvent

untestabilityReason.justification: A single POST with no branching. The event kinds it may carry are enforced server-side by isUserEventKind, covered by app/lib/exchange.test.ts, and the answered path it serves is covered by answeredResponse in app/lib/toolInvocation.test.ts.

description: Recognises a Prisma known-request error structurally - a string code beside a string clientVersion - and returns the code, or null. Deliberately not instanceof: the thrown value has usually crossed a server component boundary by the time it is classified, and may come from a different copy of the client than this module imports, so class identity is not something to bet the error screen on. Requiring clientVersion as well as code is what stops a Node system error (ENOENT, which also has a code) being dressed up as a Prisma diagnosis.
name: prismaCode

description: Publishes a headless driver on window over the same bound catalog. Not a debug convenience: WebMCP is top-level-secure-context only and codeyam renders the app inside a capture iframe, so navigator.modelContext is genuinely absent in every preview and captured scenario, and this driver is what makes the tools exercisable there at all. It calls the exact catalog entries a real agent would.
name: publishAgentDriver

description: The node ids a question.asked event announced. Tolerates a malformed or absent payload, because the log carries untrusted JSON that may predate the current shape.
name: questionIds

description: Turns the raw exchange log into the lines the activity rail shows, oldest first. Composes the three rules below: drop the bookkeeping, collapse runs, word what is left.
name: railEntries

description: Reads whatever a brief route answered with, from the browser: status before body, the route's own sentence preferred over a generic one, an omitted warning spelled as null rather than undefined, and never a parse error reaching a person. A 200 whose body carries no text is treated as the failure it is. Exists because the landing card and the older intake were each doing this independently, and two copies of one contract is one copy away from drifting.
name: readBriefResponse

description: Validates a drawn shape a language model asked for, on its way into the map. A shape that cannot be drawn — fewer than two steps once blanks are dropped, or not an object at all — becomes null rather than a half-formed diagram, because a card announcing a shape and then showing nothing is worse than one that never claimed to have it. The note is omitted entirely rather than carried empty, since the card renders a caption line for anything truthy.
name: readDiagram

description: Reads a fetch response whose body might not be JSON, and never lets JSON.parse throw at a person. Consumes the body as text once, then returns the data on success, the route's own stated error on a failing JSON body, and '<fallback> (HTTP <status>)' for an empty, truncated, or HTML body. Reports ok only when the caller actually got usable data, so a 200 carrying a truncated body reads as the failure it is. Pure over a Response, so it is testable with a constructed one and no network.
name: readJson

description: The refs an insight cites, normalised and ready for the resolution pass applyToolCalls performs. Strings only, blanks dropped, and an empty result turned to null - the same shape serialiseOptions uses and for the same reason: a node that named nothing should be indistinguishable from one that never had the field, rather than carrying an empty array nobody can render. Non-strings are filtered rather than stringified, because turning 42 into '42' would store a citation pointing at nothing while looking like it had worked.
name: readRefs

description: Everything that happened after a cursor. An omitted cursor means the whole log, which is what a fresh agent wants; a cursor means just the delta, which is what a returning one wants. Both return the map's current revision, so a caller always leaves holding a cursor it can resume from even when the delta is empty.
name: readSince

description: The only place a map revision is minted. Appends events to the map's log and bumps ThinkingMap.revision once per event inside a single transaction, so a revision can never exist without its event or vice versa - either would hand a reader a cursor it cannot resume from. Every row of a batch carries the requestId, so a retry returns the whole original batch and its LAST revision; keying only the first row loses the batch's extent and hands a retrying agent a stale cursor, which makes it re-read its own writes as new. The dedupe lookup itself lives in findPriorBatch, shared with applyToolCalls so there is one notion of "seen this key". Takes an optional transaction client: a caller already inside a transaction hands over its own, because SQLite will not nest transactions and opening a second would deadlock against the write lock the outer one holds. Fires the in-process emitter that waiting callers race against - but NOT when a transaction was borrowed, since the outer transaction has not committed yet and waking a waiter on a revision that can still roll back would show a map that never existed.
name: recordEvents

description: Renders the log one line per event: revision, kind, origin, and the gist. Because the exchange is pull-only, this text is the whole of what an agent learns about what happened while it was not looking. The revision leads each line because it is what the agent passes back as its cursor, and the gist is pulled from whichever payload field that kind uses.
name: renderEvents

description: Closes the open questions an answer resolved, logging one node.updated per node that actually moved. Answering the same question twice logs the second answer without inventing a second change, and a node the agent has since deleted is skipped rather than failing the write.
name: resolveAnswered

description: The cited nodes an insight can actually point at, resolved against the node set. Dangling ids are DROPPED rather than throwing or rendering as a blank - the same tolerance testsNodeId is documented to have, for the same reason: the node an insight named may since have been deleted, and an insight that stopped reading because one of its sources is gone would be a worse outcome than one citing fewer sources than it once did.
name: resolveCitations

description: Turns a ref into the id it names. A ref is one of two things and the caller cannot tell which: a temporary name minted earlier in this same plan, or the real id of something already on the board - so resolution tries the plan first and falls through to the value itself. The load-bearing half is that an unresolvable value is returned UNCHANGED rather than dropped: a dangling link is reported on screen, whereas silently discarding it would hide that the node claimed a relationship at all. Hoisted out of four identical inline sites in applyToolCalls (parentRef, testsRef, themeRef, and the update id).
name: resolveRef

description: The readable part of an MCP tool response — the first text block, which is what an agent would actually read. Falls back to raw JSON rather than rendering nothing, because a silently empty panel is worse than an ugly one.
name: resultText

description: The line above a row, naming what the round was. A round that is entirely questions says so, because the question count is what the person is being asked to deal with; a mixed round counts nodes instead, since naming the majority kind would misdescribe it. The opening round is named for the idea rather than numbered. A research round is the exception that says what it IS rather than how many of anything it holds - what already exists is the thing somebody scanning the column is looking for, and a node count is not.
name: roundEyebrow

description: How far through a round the person is — the definition the whole feature gates on: the footer's count, whether the next row is reached for, and whether the phase's action appears. Counts only ANSWERABLE cards: a goal or assumption the agent has not filled in carries status 'open' and shows in the map caption, but has no answer box, so counting it would leave the loop permanently one short and the next row never reached for.
name: roundProgress

description: Whether a line of thinking has been answered through, which is what decides if its line to the conclusion is drawn at all. A row is done when it has questions and none is still open; an empty row is deliberately not done, because every question being answered is vacuously true of no questions and would run a conclusion line off a row nobody has said anything in. Insights do not count either way — nobody was asked them.
name: rowDone

description: How far a collapsible run of adds or updates extends from an index. An agent turn that writes six nodes is one thing that happened, not six. Returns 1 for anything not collapsible, so the caller can always advance by the result.
name: runLength

description: Validates and runs one catalog tool. Agent input is untrusted, so it is checked against the tool's own schema before reaching an implementation and a validation failure comes back as readable text. isError is reserved for genuine faults: a conflict or a timeout is a normal result the agent is expected to reason about, and flagging those as errors would invite the blind retry the conflict path exists to prevent. Every front door - page, HTTP, stdio - ends here, which is what stops the three drifting apart.
name: runTool

description: Cuts the log's node-adds into runs, starting a new one whenever the writing side changes or the revisions stop being contiguous. A non-add event between two adds breaks contiguity, which is exactly right: ask_user writes its questions and then a question.asked, so a later add_nodes is genuinely a later turn.
name: runsFromLog

description: Builds one BriefSection from an index, a heading and a body - trimming the body and deriving its character count so the outline can be trusted without any passage being read.
name: section

description: Renders a brief section id as a person reads it - s7 becomes the section mark for 7. The id is the address the splitter derives, a node stores in sourceRef, and read_brief takes; the mark is only ever its display. Extracted from four inline copies across three components, which was three chances for the brief panel and a node pill to call the same section two different things.
name: sectionLabel

description: A mulberry32 PRNG keyed off a theme's hue, so a galaxy's dust is the same on the server and in the browser. The determinism is the load-bearing part rather than the randomness: lose it and React finds a different tree than the one the server sent, which is a hydration error on a board that otherwise looks fine. Not exported — the property is asserted through the markup it produces, since that is what actually has to match.
name: seeded

description: Turns a model's suggested answers into the JSON array the column stores, dropping the field entirely unless at least one usable string survives — so an agent sending an empty list or a list of blanks produces a plain question rather than a node carrying an array nothing can render. Non-strings are filtered rather than coerced, because a numeric option is a mistake and stringifying it would hide one.
name: serialiseOptions

description: The sentence the bounded shimmer resolves into, for each of the three things that can be true about who can hear the log: an agent mid-turn has what was added, an agent is attached but not in a turn, or nothing can reach the page at all. The three are deliberately distinct claims — collapsing them would make the page sound more attended-to than it is. Says what you have added rather than your answers, because the same row appears on a day-one map that has only a seed idea. Exported so the isolated-component fixtures cite the real sentence instead of a hand-copy that can drift.
name: settledNote

description: Truncates an attachment name for a chip that must not grow wide enough to push the first card's own controls out of line, keeping the ellipsis inside the budget rather than adding it on top. A page title runs to a sentence far more often than a filename does, which is what made this necessary once links could be attached.
name: shorten

description: Splits an assistant reply into renderable lines and marks the ones that are questions, so the conversation panel can give them typographic weight. Only a line ending in a question mark counts; a mid-sentence question mark is usually the partner quoting the person back.
name: splitAssistantLines

description: Cuts a brief into stable, addressable sections - s1..sN with a heading, body and character count each. Splits on markdown headings where the document has them and groups paragraphs to a target size where it does not. Pure, so the same immutable text always yields the same ids without a table to keep in sync; an empty document returns no sections rather than one empty one.
name: splitIntoSections

description: Splits a document on its markdown headings, one section per heading. Prose before the first heading becomes its own section rather than being dropped - it is usually the summary - and a heading with nothing under it is kept, because a section the client left empty is part of the document's shape.
name: splitOnHeadings

description: Groups paragraphs up to a target size when a document has no headings, so plain prose still comes back as a readable handful of passages. A single paragraph over the maximum is left whole: an oversized passage beats one severed mid-argument.
name: splitOnParagraphs

description: The standing ask as numbers, carried on read_map's structured output so an agent reading structured results does not have to parse the prose back into the figures it is being asked to compare itself against. The insights themselves are deliberately NOT included - they are already in the map the same call rendered, and repeating them would double the size of every read.
name: standing

description: The instruction half of the standing ask - what the agent is being asked to do, as opposed to what the board currently holds. Separate from the counts because the two change for different reasons and at different rates: the numbers move every turn, this sentence moves when the product decides what an insight is for. Built by interpolating INSIGHT_STREAM_KINDS and TARGET_LIVE_INSIGHTS rather than typed out, so a kind added to the stream cannot end up described to the agent by a list that no longer matches the one the code counts.
name: standingAskSentence

description: Picks the one readable field worth showing for an event, in preference order - label, then text, then phase, then answer. Each event kind carries its human-readable part under a different name, and an agent reading a wall of bare kinds learns nothing about what changed.
name: summarize

description: Renders the current map as an indented outline carrying each node's real id, kind and status. This is the context the model reads before every turn, and the ids are what let it target an existing node with update_node.
name: summarizeMap

description: Holds text selection off for the duration of a drag and returns the restore function. Scoped to the gesture rather than the map, because selecting a node's label is worth keeping — it is how you copy one out.
name: suppressTextSelection

description: Wraps a string in the content envelope every MCP tool response takes. A one-line shape adapter with no branches; the strings it wraps are built by mcpFormat.
name: textResult

untestabilityReason.justification: A single return statement building the SDK's response literal - no branches, no transformation. The text it wraps comes from formatMapList and formatMapDetail, both covered by app/lib/mcpFormat.test.ts, and the envelope shape itself was verified against a live MCP client over both transports.

description: A theme's hue as a CSS colour at a given lightness, saturation and alpha. One place decides what a theme looks like so a card, its connector and its cluster label cannot drift apart. Emits no alpha channel when the colour is opaque, because an always-present slash-one would be valid CSS that changed every colour string in the app for nothing.
name: themeColor

description: How deep a thread bends, given the vertical gap between two rows: two thirds of the gap, clamped at both ends. The floor exists because a straight line between two rows reads as a table rule rather than a thread; the ceiling exists because past it the control points overshoot their own endpoints and the curve loops back on itself. Between the clamps the bend tracks the gap, so a taller gap gets a lazier curve rather than the same one stretched.
name: threadPull

description: Clamps an agent's requested wait into milliseconds: a default when none is given, a ceiling so a confused agent cannot pin a connection open indefinitely, and a one-second floor so a wait never degrades into a busy loop.
name: timeoutMsFrom

description: The catalog as a browser agent or the headless driver lists it. A tool missing here is a tool the agent never learns it can call, so it is derived from the catalog rather than restated.
name: toolSummaries

description: The sentence a person sends the agent when they notice a brief section nobody has dealt with. It rides the existing user.note channel, so the wording IS the whole message - nothing else carries the intent. It names the section twice over, by mark and by heading, so the agent can go straight to it rather than re-reading the outline, and it asks a question rather than only reporting an absence, because the point is to get the section dealt with on the next turn.
name: untouchedNoteText

description: Moving the map to its next phase, from the page — the first page-side caller of set_phase, which until now only ever moved because an agent moved it. The ORDER is the point: the note saying what was decided goes on the log BEFORE the phase moves, so an agent reading the log finds a sentence rather than a phase that silently changed under it. A failed phase write therefore leaves the decision recorded, and says so rather than claiming the note was lost.
name: useAdvancePhase

description: The ask_user promise lifecycle: park an agent's turn on a set of questions, and release it when they are answered or the clock runs out. Separate from the log because it is a different clock — the log is durable and outlives everyone, this is one turn held in memory. A second ask releases the first as unanswered rather than stranding its promise.
name: useAskUser

description: Pan and zoom over the board, held as one piece of state so a scale and a translation landing in different renders cannot make the board visibly shear. The load-bearing detail is that the pointer is NOT captured on pointerdown but only after a few pixels of travel: capturing early retargets the eventual click to the canvas, which silently made every card on the board unclickable. Drag deltas are divided by the current scale so the board tracks the cursor identically at every zoom, and the scale is clamped at both ends so it can never invert or collapse.
name: useBoardCamera

description: How long something has been true, reported once it has been true long enough — the only input the pending row needs that a pure function cannot compute. Reports a STEP rather than a ticking clock, 0 until the limit then the limit, because a value changing every frame would re-render the whole map column to move a decision that flips exactly once. Restarts on its reset key, so a new round means the page is reaching for something new rather than still waiting on the old.
name: useBoundedWait

description: The page's own copy of the exchange log, kept current. Polls the log forward from the cursor it holds — the same way an agent reads it, because WebMCP is pull-only and there is no push channel — and re-renders the server component when the log moves past what was rendered, so the server-rendered map does not sit out of step with its own log.
name: useExchangeLog

description: Keeping the bottom of a growing column in view, for a reader who is already at the bottom and nobody else. Two subtleties: it must not fire on first paint, because a page that jumps to its own bottom before the person has read the top is not reacting to anything; and 'have I run before' is the wrong way to express that, since StrictMode invokes effects twice on mount and would consume such a flag — so the refs are seeded with mount-time values during render and the effect compares against a transition instead.
name: useFollowColumn

description: What every question on the map has been answered, and how to answer one. Merges the log's answers with an optimistic layer for answers written in this tab: the answer takes the card's body the moment it is sent, because one still sitting in the input after you pressed send reads as the answer having been lost, and it is rolled back only if the write actually failed. The pending entry is never cleared on success — the log catches up on its own, and clearing early would flicker the question back to unanswered.
name: useMapAnswers

description: The bridge if there is one, null if there is not. For a component that renders in both the app and an isolated scenario, where the throwing accessor would make the second case a crash rather than a state. Anything that genuinely needs the exchange still uses useWebMcpBridge and says so by throwing.
name: useOptionalWebMcpBridge

untestabilityReason.justification: a single useContext read with no branching logic; the state it returns is exercised through the components that consume it

description: Reads the bridge state - connection status, the questions an agent is waiting on, the current revision, and the two writers - from context. Throws outside a provider rather than returning a null the caller would have to guard at every use site.
name: useWebMcpBridge

untestabilityReason.justification: A useContext read with a single null check and no other branching. The state it exposes is produced by the WebMcpBridge component, which is covered by the mid-exchange scenario.

description: Parses a dotted-quad IPv4 address into a 32-bit integer, or null when it is not one, so the CIDR checks in isBlockedAddress are mask arithmetic rather than string comparison. Rejects out-of-range octets and non-numeric parts rather than coercing them.
name: v4ToInt

description: Checks an agent's call against the tool it named and returns either the parsed input or the response to send back. Runs on the page as well as the server - not redundantly, but because it turns a malformed call into an immediate readable answer rather than a round trip, and agent input is untrusted on both sides of the wire. The message names the offending field so the agent can correct itself instead of guessing.
name: validateToolInput

description: The events worth showing a person, with the bookkeeping dropped. Hides the open-question nodes that ask_user created when a question.asked announced them, and the node.updated that closes a question the person just answered — both are cases where one act produced two events. An agent's own update to the same node still shows.
name: visibleEvents

description: Blocks until somebody starts a thinking map, or until the caller's timeout expires. The server-door half of the answer to a page not being able to wake an agent: nothing here pushes, but an agent with nothing to do can park, so a submitted idea is picked up rather than sitting on an empty page. A near-copy of waitForUserActivity - check first, then race the in-process emitter against a poll, on a bounded deadline - so the two read as one pattern. Cursored by createdAt rather than revision, because revision is per-map and a map that does not exist yet has none a waiter could have read. The comparison is exclusive, which is what stops a re-park from re-delivering the map just handed over. A timeout is a normal result carrying the cursor, never an error.
name: waitForNewMap

description: Blocks until the person contributes, or until the caller's timeout expires. Re-reads the log first because an event may already be waiting and a waiter that subscribed before checking would sleep through it; then races an in-process emitter against a ~500ms poll. The poll is what lets a write from the separate stdio process wake a waiter living in the web process - an emitter alone would be silently correct in dev and silently wrong across front doors. Always resolves: a timeout is a normal result carrying the cursor, never a hang.
name: waitForUserActivity

description: Why the page is not bound, in words the UI can show honestly. Each reason names a different fix, so they deliberately do not collapse into one generic unavailable the person cannot act on. The security gates are reported before the missing-agent gate so an insecure page is told to fix that first.
name: webMcpUnavailableReason

description: Names the side that acted — 'Agent' or 'You'. The map is co-authored, so every rail line has to attribute itself; an unrecognised origin falls through as itself rather than becoming an anonymous row.
name: who

description: How wide a card needs to be, driven by what it carries rather than declared by the agent: a card holding a drawn shape or a picture gets the wide column, everything else the standard one. Letting the model describe content and the board decide the room it takes is what stops every card becoming a layout negotiation. Not exported — its rule is asserted through the placements layOutGalaxy produces, which is the thing that actually matters: a card that gained a diagram but kept the narrow column squeezes its content into a strip.
name: widthFor

description: Wraps a Next route handler so an unanticipated throw becomes a JSON 500 rather than an unparseable body. Logs the original error to the terminal, runs it through classifyLoadError, and answers { error, command?, hint?, detail? } with the fix and the internals present only in development. A handler's own response passes through untouched, so a deliberate 400 or 404 keeps its status and body. Variadic so it composes with both (request) and (request, { params }) handlers without casting.
name: withFailure

description: Opens an extracted page with its own title as a markdown heading, skipping it when the article already starts with that title so the name is not said twice before the first sentence. Restores something extraction dropped rather than inventing it — without it a board started from a Wikipedia article was named 'From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia', identical for every article on the site.
name: withTitleHeading
